articles.title: Gold Edges Up, Still On Track for Worst Weekly Slump Since June
articles.excerpt:
(Bloomberg) -- Gold edged higher at the end of a downbeat week that saw the metal drop to its lowest point in more than a year.

Bullion rose slightly to trade just below $3,900 an ounce. Prices briefly hit a 13-month low on Thursday as investors ramped up bets on the Federal Reserve raising interest rates. Yields on some Treasuries surged by more than 12 basis points in the previous session, with the biggest increases seen in short-term securities that are more sensitive to changes in central bank policy.

articles.title: Yen Falls to Cusp of 160 Level, Fanning Intervention Risk
articles.excerpt:
(Bloomberg) -- The yen slid to the verge of 160 to the dollar, a key threshold that’s raising the specter that policymakers in Tokyo will swoop in again to defend the currency.

As rising US bond yields pushed the dollar higher, the yen slipped 0.1% to 159.94. It marked the third straight daily decline as traders brace for the Federal Reserve to step up its interest rate hikes, giving investors an incentive to shift cash to the US as yields surge further above those in Japan.

articles.title: The Yen Is Becoming Too Hard for Some Investors to Trade
articles.excerpt:
(Bloomberg) -- After a year of wild swings, the yen surprised traders by settling into a tight range clustered near 158 per dollar over recent months. But on Wednesday it broke out again, unexpectedly weakening toward 160.

The sudden move underscores just how difficult Japan’s currency has become to trade. Traditional signals such as interest-rate differentials have become less reliable guides, while Bank of Japan tightening, persistent capital outflows and unprecedented intervention have pulled the yen in competing directions.
